LESSON MENU
FILE INSTRUCTIONSLE
File instructions are used to copy or fill data files with specific values. These instructions are useful and very similar to the move instructions you learned earlier.
DISCUSSION
The difference is that these instructions can do more than just move a word. They can copy as little as a word or as much as a file..
There are only two file instructions. Let's look at these instructions and what they do.
This is the File Copy (COP) instruction. As the name implies, this instruction is used to copy files.
Note: Does not change arithmetic status bit.

The File Copy instruction requires three parameters: a source, a destination, and a length. The source is the location of a file that you want to copy. You cannot enter a data value here. (Use the move instruction for doing that.) You must enter a file location...
The second parameter is the destination location. Again, this is the file where you would like the source data copied to. Again, this parameter has to be a file location in memory.
The last element is the length. This is the number of data elements you want copied from the source into the destination. A data element has a number of words depending on the type of data...
For example, a counter data element is composed of three words, while an integer data element contains one word.

The length refers to the number of elements in the destination. For example, if you had a source as integer 0 in integer file 17 (#N17:0), a destination as counter 1 in counter file 5 (#C5:1), and a length of 2 elements, six words would be copied into the destination...

Since a counter element is three words long, a length of two elements specifies six words will be copied. If we switch the source and destination, only two words are transferred into the integer file...
These two words are the first two of the three words in counter 1. Remember, the element size is determined by the destination.
The length that you can specify depends on the number of words in the element. The maximum length value you can use must be equal to or less than 128 words.

If the destination contains integers, the maximum length is 128. If the destination contains counter data file elements, the maximum length is 42. Remember, 42 elements x 3 words per element equals 126 words...
This leaves 2 words, but a counter file has 3. This is why only 42 can be specified.

The File Copy instruction where length 1 works the same as the move instruction except that the File Copy instruction does not change the arithmetic status bits. If you need to move data without changing the arithmetic status bits, use the File Copy instruction...
The number of words in an element is determined by _______.
Remember, it is the destination that determines the word length of elements.
TRY AGAIN!
The last of the file instructions is the File Fill (FLL) instruction. This instruction is used to fill a defined number of destination elements with the same value.
Note: Does not change arithmetic status bit.

This instruction requires a source, destination, and length, just as with the File Copy instruction. The source is either an entered value or the location of a value in memory. Recall the COP instruction was restricted to a location only...
The destination is where you want the source value copied to. The length specifies how many elements of the destination will be filled with same source value.

After the instruction is evaluated, the source value is placed in the file location specified by the destination, and each element therefore, up to the length specified. Again, the maximum length is 128 words...
This instruction is very useful if you want to initialize memory with a specific value, like zero.
The source of the File Fill Instruction must be a file location. Entered values cannot be used.
Remember, the source can be either a location in memory or an actual value entered into the instruction.
TRY AGAIN!
You have examined the file instructions for a PLC..........
In the experiment, we will look at the copy command and see how it copies a large block of data.
This completes the information on FILE INSTRUCTIONS........

1. The File Copy (COP) instruction is used to copy data from one file to another and requires a source, destination, and length. The length and destination element type determine how many words will be copied.
Note: Does not change arithmetic status bit.

2. The File Fill (FLL) instruction is used to copy single values into multiple elements of a destination data file. The number of words filled with the source value is determined by the length parameter and the destination element type.
Note: Does not change arithmetic status bit.

Definition
The program shown below is the ladder logic program you will enter to demonstrate the file instructions that you learned in the first part of this lesson.
Before we actually begin entering the program into the PLC
APS software, let's look at what the program should do. This
will help us understand if the program is operating properly when we test it...
On the 5050-1 PC card, there are three switches we will use for this program: two push button switches and a slide switch.
The slide switch, which is connected to input I:0/2, is used to select between the File Copy and the File Fill instructions. This allows us to see the operation of both instructions.
When the slide switch is in the right position, rung 1 is active. This rung uses the copy command to copy the inputs of one word starting at I:0.0 to one word of output O:0.0.
If we press the START or STOP buttons, the corresponding output LEDs should illuminate. Also, the slide switch LED,
LED 2, should remain illuminated as long as the switch is on.
If the slide switch is in the left position, the output file's first word will have highs in each bit. This causes the LEDs to remain illuminated. Notice that we are using the entered value -1.

Remember, negative values are stored in two's-complement form. The binary value for negative 1 is 1111111111111111. When you enter the instructions later, you can enter negative one as -1, &HFFFF or &B1111111111111111. All of these represent the same value.
The operation of these instructions is straightforward. We have implemented them into our short program so that you can observe their performance.

When used in larger programs, these instructions are similarly implemented, except, in most cases, the length value will be greater. Since we can only display half of the first word of the output, it isn't necessary to copy more...
